S09.basis: No reservoir or inlet is evidenced on site, so the step is conditional on the reservoir of S08; water standing at the level of a pavement-level reservoir stops 21.7 m below the top of the well shaft and 51.5 m below the Gallery roof, a head that the pump of S10 must supply.

S10.basis: The hypothesis names no actuator or seal for the pump, which must push with 0.43 to 1.01 MN depending on its position and hold 0.80 MPa with the Gallery full.

S11.basis: The suction margin of a pump at the foot of the Descending Passage is -5.9 m at the Old Kingdom flood peak and -0.4 m at the most favourable documented levels, against the 0 m it needs to draw.

S12.basis: Filling the Gallery alone takes 4.3 strokes (3.9 to 4.7 over the ranges of the inputs) if a stroke sweeps the whole Descending Passage, 5.9 (5.4 to 6.4) if it sweeps the part below the Ascending Passage junction and 6.7 (6.2 to 7.3) if it sweeps the part below the pavement, against the 4 claimed, and the hypothesis fixes no stroke.

S20.basis: In one day, taken as the cycle because the hypothesis states none, the oxygen dissolved in the Gallery water and the oxygen crossing its still surface can oxidise 2.5 percent of a full batch (2.1 to 2.8 percent over the ranges of the inputs), below the 5 percent under which the criterion fails the claim and the 50 percent from which it passes it; a still surface would need 27 days (22 to 302 days over the ranges of the inputs) to bring the yield to 5 percent, and the hypothesis describes no aeration.

S21.basis: If the first of the 4 claimed fills took the whole heat of the largest batch, it would warm by 7.3 K and leave a margin of 72.7 K below boiling (62.3 K at the least), so nothing boils over with or without the dilute-acid step.

S25.basis: A slab driven at the air-breakdown field emits 50 dB and the path to the north slab loses 101 dB at 13 kHz, so the signal arrives at -51 dB (-55 dB at the least), against the 10 dB needed above a 0 dB noise floor.

S27.basis: Hydrogen chloride stands at 1.2e-07 atm over the dilute acid and salt mixture, and at 1.5e-07 atm over saturated brine, against the 1e-05 atm below which the criterion fails the claim.

S28.basis: A vein must conduct 2.7e+05 times better than the rock to carry current 100 m; the best measured specular hematite reaches 3.3e+04 times in 100 ohm m rock and 1.0e+06 times in the most resistive 3000 ohm m rock, earthy red hematite reaches 4.2e-02 times at most, and no Giza vein has been measured.

S29.basis: A vein must conduct 2.7e+05 times better than the rock to carry current 100 m; the best measured specular hematite reaches 3.3e+04 times in 100 ohm m rock and 1.0e+06 times in the most resistive 3000 ohm m rock, earthy red hematite reaches 4.2e-02 times at most, and no Giza vein has been measured.

S30.basis: Pure sulfur dioxide at one atmosphere caps the product at 0.023 mol/L (0.026 mol/L at most), or 0.012 mol/L if its oxygen comes with the same draw of air, below the 0.05 mol/L pass line at any gas fraction; the ceiling scales with the sulfur dioxide fraction of the chamber gas, so the product stays above the 0.005 mol/L fail line only if that fraction is at least 22 percent (19 percent with every input at its favourable end), and the hypothesis states no gas fraction.

S31.basis: Direct strikes come at most 0.12 times per year, one every 8 years, and the hypothesis states no cycle rate to compare this with.
